tool_input.command:
cat > .tmp/missions/daemon-harness-impl.yaml <<'YAML'
leader: claude
worker: bwk
evaluator:
  handle: rsc
inputs:
  ticket: beadle-gi5t
write_set:
  - internal/testenv/ethos.go
  - internal/testenv/daemon.go
  - internal/daemon/harness_test.go
  - internal/daemon/pipeline_test.go
  - .github/workflows/test.yml
  - Makefile
  - docs/TESTING.md
context: |
  Implement the daemon test harness specified in docs/daemon-test-harness.md.
  Read that document end to end first -- it went through two review rounds
  with an evaluator and its decisions are load-bearing, not suggestions.

  WHY THIS EXISTS. beadle-daemon's mail path (email -> trust classification
  -> per-contact permission -> planner -> executor -> runner -> ethos mission
  create -> worker spawn) had never actually run until a manual live test.
  That one run surfaced four real defects, including a mission-contract shape
  ethos's real schema rejects outright -- every daemon-triggered mission would
  have failed. Everything since has been building the ability to catch that
  class automatically.

  THE HARD CONSTRAINT, from which most of the design follows: dev/CI parity,
  no environment-dependent branches.
    - No t.Skip on a missing dependency. If a required tool is absent the test
      FAILS with a message naming what to install. A test that silently skips
      locally is the same failure as one that skips in CI -- that is exactly
      how the contract-schema bug shipped.
    - One entry point. The tier runs under `make check`; CI invokes that same
      target. No CI-only invocation, no separate flag or build tag.
    - Zero dependence on ambient developer state.
    - Fast enough to sit in a pre-commit gate.

  MATERIAL THAT ALREADY EXISTS -- this is mostly composition, not new
  infrastructure. Survey before building anything:
    - internal/testserver.Fixture: in-process IMAP+SMTP, no real network.
      AddRawMessage(folder, raw []byte) takes arbitrary RFC822, so any trust
      level can be induced directly -- Proton internal headers for `trusted`,
      a real multipart/signed body for verified/untrusted, neither for
      unverified.
    - internal/testenv.Env: AddContact(name, addr, permissions) writes the
      per-contact rwx grants gate 2 turns on. AddIdentity, WriteConfig.
    - internal/testenv/gpg.go: GenKey, GenKeyNoExpiry, GenKeyWithPassphrase,
      ShortGPGHome, IsolateTempDir -- ephemeral keyrings for gate 3.
    - internal/daemon.Spawner is an interface; WorkerSpawner is the only
      implementation and it execs a real `claude` subprocess. That single seam
      is the one thing that stays faked.
    - isolatedEthosEnv in internal/daemon/pipeline_test.go: the established
      real-ethos-CLI isolation pattern. Its filter is
      `strings.HasPrefix(kv, "HOME=") || strings.HasPrefix(kv, "ETHOS_")`.
      Port it to testenv preserving that property -- no ETHOS_* ambient leak.

  FOUR GATES, each with its negative case:
    1. Trust classification -- OnNewMail admits only Verified/Trusted; the
       lower rungs create nothing.
    2. Per-contact `x` permission -- a perfectly verified message from an
       ungranted sender unlocks nothing.
    3. Command-file signature -- unsigned, wrong-key, and expired-key files
       all rejected when an owner key is configured. NOTE the design's
       rescope: the absent/ambiguous-daemon.json case lives in
       cmd/beadle-daemon and already has coverage; do not duplicate it.
    4. Contract validity against the REAL ethos CLI -- the gate the schema bug
       broke, catchable only by a real exec. Includes a NEGATIVE control: a
       deliberately malformed contract asserted REJECTED. That control exists
       to catch a systemic harness failure (broken isolation, PATH
       misconfiguration, a swallowed error) that would make every
       `ethos mission create` spuriously succeed. Without it, gate 4's only
       assertion is success, which a broken harness satisfies trivially.

  DRIVE OnNewMail DIRECTLY, not the Poller. Poller's first poll never fires
  the new-mail callback and its minimum interval is 1m, so a pre-commit test
  cannot wait on it. Poller has no security-relevant logic of its own; the
  gates all live in OnNewMail and downstream. This is testing the right layer,
  not working around a timing problem.

  ETHOS PROVISIONING: ETHOS_VERSION := v4.16.0, installed via
  `go install github.com/punt-labs/ethos/v4/cmd/ethos@$(ETHOS_VERSION)`.
  Verified working against a clean module cache. Wire it as a real prerequisite
  so `make check` provisions it rather than a developer running a manual step,
  and add the matching CI step per the design.
success_criteria:
  - All four gates covered, each with the negative case the design names, driven through the real OnNewMail entry point
  - Gate 4 includes the malformed-contract negative control, and it is demonstrated to FAIL if the contract is made valid -- prove the control can fail, do not just assert it passes
  - No t.Skip anywhere in the tier; a missing dependency produces a failure naming what to install
  - The tier runs under `make check` with no separate flag or build tag, and CI invokes that same target
  - The ported isolation helper strips every ETHOS_* variable, not only ETHOS_REPO_ROOT, and no test mutates the real ~/.punt-labs/ethos tree -- verify by snapshotting before and after a full run
  - Spawner is the only faked seam; every other component is the real one
  - Each gate's negative case is confirmed to fail when the guard it tests is removed -- a gate test that passes with its own protection disabled proves nothing
  - go test -race -count=1 ./... passes; test count does not decrease
  - make check passes with zero suppressions
  - docs/TESTING.md gains the tier, describing what it covers, what a new gate test costs to add, and the no-skip/one-entry-point rule
  - Commit incrementally -- one commit per logical step. Each commit must pass `make check`. Do not accumulate more than 30 minutes of uncommitted changes.
budget:
  rounds: 3
  reflection_after_each: true
